messages.subject: Re: dplyr impact on row names
messages.body_plain:
Yes, I don't remove them so you can later use add_rownames() (new in
dplyr 0.4) to convert them back to proper variables.

Hadley

On Sat, Dec 27, 2014 at 2:56 PM, Bob <muen...@tennessee.edu> wrote:
> Hi All,
>
> I've been fiddling around with dplyr & row names. Since it messes with them
> I figured a good approach was to manage id information in variables and then
> put them into the row.names position only right before you need them for a
> function that reports its values. When I did that and printed, it looked
> like they were over-written again. But that's not the case. tbl_df() doesn't
> over-write them, print.tbl_df() just hides them from you, giving you the
> impression that they've been over-written. See example below.
>
> Cheers,
> Bob
>

>> gender <- rep(c("m","f"), 100)
>> y  <- rnorm(200)
>>

>> mydata <- data.frame(id, gender, y)
>> row.names(mydata) <- id

messages.body_plain:
OneVar is just a variable of a database.

To be more specific, I'm trying to make spaghetti plots using ggplot and shiny. The data are from a retailer panel, with weekly sales for products. For each product, the data contains info on the store where it's sold, the name of the store chain, the brand, the type of product...

> names(DATA)
 [1] "store"    "weeks"    "Product"  "LogSales" "LogPrice" "sstype"   "fabr"     "marque"   "ensnum"   "circuit"
[11] "surface"

I can produce multiple plots outside of Shiny (below an example of sales by product types, "sstype" means sub-sub-type):
>D2 <- data %>%
  group_by(sstype,week) %>%
  summarise_each(funs(sum),volume)
>p2 <- ggplot(data=D2 , aes(x=week , y=volume , group=sstype , color=factor(sstype)))
>p2 + geom_line()

However, when I turn to Shiny, I get multiple issue. I tried for several hours to get it working, with no luck. Here is the last version with "paste", but I get an error message saying the object "weeks" doesn't exist
I have dplyr 0.3.0.2 and shiny 0.10.2.1
The RenderText is working fine, but graphic and table don't show up...

I am open to any suggestion or clarification

ui.R
library(shiny)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(lazyeval)
library(magrittr)

shinyUI(fluidPage(
  # Application title
  titlePanel("Spaghetti Plot For Pasta Sales"),

  # choosing explanatory factor (store, product, type, manufacturer, brand, chain, circuit)
  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
      selectInput("factor", label = "explaining factor:",
                  choices = c("store","Product","sstype","fabr","marque","ensnum","circuit"),
                  selected = "ensnum")
      ),

    # Show the factor, the plot, and the table head
    mainPanel(
      textOutput("text1"),
      plotOutput("distPlot") ,
      tableOutput("view")
    )
  )
))

server.R

library(shiny)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(lazyeval)
library(magrittr)

# server logic
shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  load(file="DATA.RData")

# print the selected factor
  output$text1 <- renderText({
    paste("You have selected", as.symbol(input$factor))
  })

# summarize and ggplot
  output$distPlot <- renderPlot({

    D <-  DATA %>%
    group_by_( input$factor , paste(weeks) )  %>%
    summarise_each(funs(sum), LogSales)

p1 <- ggplot(data = D, aes_string(x = weeks, y = LogSales , group = input$factor , color=factor(input$factor)))
p1 + geom_line() +  theme(legend.position = "none")

# print the head of table D
output$view <- renderTable({
  head(D)
})

})
})

messages.subject_clean: How to deal with functions masked by dplyr?
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

dplyr::collapse masks nlme::collapse, so I have to load dplyr after nlme in order for dplyr to work as expected.

Similarly, dplyr::select masks MASS::select, so I have to load dplyr after nlme in order for dplyr to work as expected.

I presume that the consequence of loading dplyr last is that the masked functions no longer work as expected (unless the dplyr function is a strict superset of the masked function. Given that I loaded the earlier-loaded packages (e.g. nlme and MASS) because I needed to use them, how do I use them with dplyr loaded subsequently?

Obviously, I can just call the masked functions as nlme::collapse or MASS::select, but what happens to calls to masked functions from the code within the earlier loaded package? Possibly more difficult, what about calls to masked function from other packages? For example mgcv depends on nlme, so if mgcv calls nlme::collapse and I wan to use dplyr, what should the load order be: nlme > mgcv > dplyr?

More generally, what are the potential problems when functions are masked? How do you deal with those problems? Are there any problems that can't be dealt with?

I expect this has already been dealt with somewhere. A pointer would be greatly appreciated.

Thanks

Ross

messages.body_plain:
Is there a way to make dplyr::left_join() join two tables on numeric columns, like LibreOffice Calc's vlookup(..., sort order = 1) does? While left_join() mirrors what vlookup(..., sort order = 0) does, I can't figure out an easy way to have it join on a row with the next lowest numeric value. Here's a toy example:

grade.book <- data.frame(
  PERSON = c("Bobby", "Jane", "Johnny", "Luisa"),
  PERC = c(67.8, 78.9, 89.1, 90.2)
)

grade.scale <- data.frame(
  SCORE = c(90, 80, 70, 60, 0),
  GRADE = c("A", "B", "C", "D", "F")
)

left_join(grade.book, grade.scale, by = c("PERC" = "SCORE"))

  PERSON PERC GRADE
1  Bobby 67.8  <NA>
2   Jane 78.9  <NA>
3 Johnny 89.1  <NA>
4  Luisa 90.2  <NA>

But, I'd like it to give me:

  PERSON PERC GRADE
1  Bobby 67.8     D
2   Jane 78.9     C
3 Johnny 89.1     B
4  Luisa 90.2     A

One work-around involves two "for" loops and an "if" statement:

all.grades <- c()
for (i in 1:nrow(grade.book)) {
  cur.perc <- grade.book[i, 'PERC']
  for (j in 1:nrow(grade.scale)) {
    cur.score <- grade.scale[j, 'SCORE']
    if (cur.perc > cur.score) {
      all.grades[i] <- as.character(grade.scale$GRADE[j])
      break
    }
  } # next possible grade
} # next person in gradebook
grade.book$GRADE <- all.grades

Is there an argument in left_join() that I'm missing that might do this?

Thanks in advance for any help, even on making the work-around shorter.

> grade.scale <- data.frame(
+     SCORE = rev(c(90, 80, 70, 60, 0)),
+     GRADE = rev(c("A", "B", "C", "D", "F"))
+ )
> grade.book %>% mutate(GRADE=cut(PERC,c(grade.scale$SCORE,100),labels=grade.scale$GRADE))

  PERSON PERC GRADE
1  Bobby 67.8     D
2   Jane 78.9     C
3 Johnny 89.1     B
4  Luisa 90.2     A

More generally, as long as the "labels" are unique to the rows in the grade.scale,
I think you can implement the non equi-join by inner joining the above result back with grade.scale (e.g).

> grade.scale <- data.frame(
+     SCORE = rev(c(90, 80, 70, 60, 0)),
+     GRADE = rev(c("A", "B", "C", "D", "F")),
+     RETAKECLASS=rev(c("N","N","MAYBE","Y","Y"))
+ )
> grade.book %>% mutate(GRADE=cut(PERC,c(grade.scale$SCORE,100),labels=grade.scale$GRADE)) %>% inner_join(grade.scale)

Hi glad if someone can help me with this.

I want to apply a different chi-square test to subset of my data frame, inside the dplyr ecosystem.
So far the only way to have what I want is to do it separately and bind rows after.
But I am sure there is a nice way to do this.

First subset, PATTERN with "abxac":

pattern.A <- genotypes.summary %>%
  filter(PATTERN=="abxac") %>%
  group_by(LOCUS) %>%
  do(
    CHISQ=chisq.test(c(.$aa,.$ab, .$ac, .$bc), p = c(0.25, 0.25, 0.25, 0.25), simulate.p.value=T, B=1000)
    ) %>%
  mutate(
    GOF = CHISQ$statistic,
    GOF_PVALUE = CHISQ$p.value
    ) %>%
  select(-CHISQ)

Second subset, PATTERN with "abxab":

pattern.B <- genotypes.summary %>%
  filter(PATTERN=="abxab") %>%
  group_by(LOCUS) %>%
  do(
    CHISQ=chisq.test(c(.$aa,.$ab, .$bb), p = c(0.25, 0.5, 0.25))
    ) %>%
  mutate(
    GOF = CHISQ$statistic,
    GOF_PVALUE = CHISQ$p.value
    ) %>%
  select(-CHISQ)

Third subset, PATTERN with "aaxab" and "abxaa":

pattern.D <- genotypes.summary %>%
  filter(PATTERN=="aaxab" | PATTERN=="abxaa") %>%
  group_by(LOCUS) %>%
  do(
    CHISQ=chisq.test(c(.$aa,.$ab), p = c(0.5,0.5))
    ) %>%
  mutate(
    GOF = CHISQ$statistic,
    GOF_PVALUE = CHISQ$p.value
    ) %>%
  select(-CHISQ)

The only thing different between the 3 subset of "genotypes.summary" is the CHISQ test (goodness of fit) applied to the subset "abxac" and "abxab" (in bold).

pattern.A, pattern.B and pattern.D  return data frames with 3 columns that could be bind by rows (the chi-square is applied by rows (by LOCUS))

Question: I sure there is a nicer and shorter way to apply the different CHISQ to the data set at once?

Thanks
Thierry

messages.body_plain:
I think this problem is most naturally frame as having two tables of
data: one at the item level and one at the transaction level.

library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)

items <- structure(list(receipt = structure(c(1L, 1L, 1L, 2L, 2L, 3L,

  3L, 3L, 3L, 4L, 4L, 4L, 4L, 4L, 4L), .Label = c("receipt1", "receipt2",
    "receipt3", "receipt4"), class = "factor"), item = structure(c(2L,
      1L, 3L, 3L, 4L, 2L, 1L, 3L, 4L, 2L, 1L, 3L, 4L, 5L, 6L), .Label
= c("pants",
        "shirt", "socks", "shoes", "belt", "hat"), class = "factor"),
  price = c(20, 30, 5, 5, 80, 20, 30, 5, 80, 20, 30, 5, 80,
    20, 25)), .Names = c("receipt", "item", "price"), row.names = c(NA,
      -15L), class = "data.frame")

receipts <- items %>%
  group_by(receipt) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), price = sum(price))

# What was the average amount spent?

receipts %>% mutate(avg = price / n)

# What receipts included a belt?
receipts %>%
  semi_join(items %>% filter(item == "belt"), by = "receipt")

# Given that someone bought a shirt, what was the average spend?
receipts %>%
  semi_join(items %>% filter(item == "shirt"), by = "receipt") %>%
  mutate(avg = price / n)
